table_title: List the top 3 highest-grossing year-leader films (by worldwide nominal gross) per decade 1980s-2020s, per Wikipedia's `List of highest-grossing films` master article's 'High-grossing films by year of release' table. The year-leader table provides predominantly 1 row per year (the highest-grossing film for that year of release; the master has rare duplicate-candidate rows for 1995 and 2005 where the staged year-leader is the master's canonical #1 selected from the candidates); top 3 per decade is computed by grouping selected year-leaders by release decade and ranking within each decade by Worldwide Gross DESC. 5 decade partitions × 3 top-ranked films per decade = 15 rows total. Schema: composite PK (Decade, Rank Within Decade) + Film + Release Year + Worldwide Gross (USD), all values master-table-verbatim except numeric gross which strips master's currency-comma formatting.
db_analog: WITH year_leaders AS (SELECT f.title, f.release_year, f.worldwide_gross_usd, FLOOR(f.release_year / 10) * 10 AS decade_start_year FROM (SELECT * FROM films_master WHERE is_year_leader_by_worldwide_gross = TRUE) f WHERE f.release_year BETWEEN 1980 AND 2025), ranked AS (SELECT title, release_year, worldwide_gross_usd, decade_start_year, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY decade_start_year ORDER BY worldwide_gross_usd DESC) AS rank_within_decade FROM year_leaders) SELECT CONCAT(decade_start_year, 's') AS decade, rank_within_decade, title AS film, release_year, worldwide_gross_usd FROM ranked WHERE rank_within_decade <= 3 ORDER BY decade_start_year ASC, rank_within_decade ASC
temporal_note: Wikipedia 'List of highest-grossing films' master article accessed 2026-05-21; staged universe FROZEN at this access time scoped to release years 1980-2025 (any live 2026 row out of scope until future re-staging pass per cycle-2 audit-recommended freeze-policy clarification). Universe = 15 films = top 3 highest-grossing year-leader films per decade across 5 decades (1980s through 2020s). Year-leader films per year come from the master's 'High-grossing films by year of release' table (predominantly 1 row per year showing the highest-grossing film released that year, with rare duplicate-candidate rows for 1995 and 2005 per cycle-1 audit observation; 1980-2025 = 46 year-leaders selected as the unambiguous #1 per year). Within each decade partition, year-leaders are sorted by Worldwide Gross DESC and top 3 kept. temporal_sensitivity = medium because (a) the 2020s decade is incomplete relative to a closed-decade scope (live 2026+ rows are OUT OF SCOPE under the 1980-2025 freeze; a future re-staging pass that extends the freeze through 2029 could shift the 2020s top 3 as additional year-leaders are admitted); (b) older-decade films' Worldwide Gross figures sometimes update due to re-releases (Avatar 2009 includes re-release revenue accumulated through 2026); (c) Wikipedia article updates can shift figures as new gross data is reported. SCOPE NOTE: the source provides predominantly year-leader films per year (1 per year, with rare 1995/2005 duplicate-candidate exceptions), so 'top 3 per decade' is computed from year-leader films — NOT from all films released in each decade. Films that were #2 or lower in their release year but might rank in their decade's top 3 are out of scope per the master's data shape. Cross-decade gap-check (cycle-2 corrected): 1980s #3 ROTJ $482M vs #4 Indiana Jones LC lower-bound $474M (gap $8M); 1990s #3 Jurassic Park $1.04B vs #4 Lion King $971M (gap $67M); 2000s #3 POTC DMC $1.07B vs #4 HP1 $1.009B (gap $57M); 2010s #3 Infinity War $2.05B vs #4 The Avengers 2012 $1.52B (gap $533M); 2020s #3 Spider-Man NWH $1.92B vs #4 Inside Out 2 $1.70B (gap $222M). Non-year-leader 2010s challengers Jurassic World 2015 $1.67B + Lion King 2019 $1.66B + non-year-leader 2020s challenger Zootopia 2 2025 $1.87B all exceed their decade's #4 year-leader but none exceed their decade's #3 staged threshold — so the 5 staged top-3-per-decade subsets are unchanged. Source priority: all values from the master article's 'High-grossing films by year of release' table — Film + Release Year + Worldwide Gross (USD) verbatim from master cells (with currency-comma formatting stripped to produce integer USD). One range-value exception: 1989 Indiana Jones LC has master gross range $474,171,806-494,000,000 which would place it #3 of 1980s at upper bound but #4 (below ROTJ $482M) at lower bound; cycle-0 used lower bound consistently so ROTJ 1983 = #3 of 1980s; documented in normalization_decisions and open_questions.
_extraction_notes: Hierarchical_decomposition instance — Decade as scaffold partition × top-3-by-gross within each decade. PIVOT context: 7th of 13 floor-lift instances toward 102-target after multiple set_filter source-friction attempts + 6 prior floor lifts (epidemics-1M lifting comparative + WWI battles lifting multi_hop + industrial-disasters lifting causal + world-expositions lifting temporal + antarctic-stations lifting set_filter + F1-champions lifting aggregation). NON-CONTINENT scaffold (Decade) per user-preference to avoid the by-continent bias in prior hierarchical instances. Brings `hierarchical_decomposition` from 5/5 (floor met, just-saturated by existing 5 instances including `top_3_best_selling_titles_per_top_5_lifetime_consoles`) to **6/5** = 7th of 13 floor-lift instances toward 102-target. Culture/Film domain existing (already extended by FilmsWinning8Oscars). artifacts/films fine-class existing (already extended). Schema: 5 cols (composite PK Decade+Rank Within Decade + Film + Release Year + Worldwide Gross). Sort: Decade ASC, Rank Within Decade ASC (1980s rank 1 → 1980s rank 2 → 1980s rank 3 → 1990s rank 1 → ... → 2020s rank 3). Per-row source: all values from master's 'High-grossing films by year of release' table — Film + Release Year + Worldwide Gross (USD) verbatim from master cells (currency-comma formatting stripped). source_count = 1 with manual_wikipedia gt_construction. claim_type = source_defined because the 15-row universe is precisely what the master's year-leader table yields when grouped by decade and filtered to top-3-by-gross within each decade. Master year-leader data limitation: source provides predominantly 1 row per year (year-leader film only, with rare 1995/2005 duplicate-candidate exceptions per cycle-1 audit observation), not multi-film-per-year — so top-3-per-decade is computed from year-leaders, NOT from all films released in the decade. Cross-decade gap-check (cycle-2 corrected for 2010s #4 = The Avengers 2012 $1.52B and 2020s/2010s non-year-leader challengers Jurassic World/Lion King/Zootopia 2) shows this limitation does not produce false negatives in the staged top-3-per-decade. Universe count = 15 (5 decades × 3 = 15 rows). 1980s gross range: $797M (E.T.) to $482M (ROTJ). 1990s: $2.26B (Titanic) to $1.04B (Jurassic Park). 2000s: $2.92B (Avatar) to $1.07B (POTC Dead Man's Chest). 2010s: $2.80B (Endgame) to $2.05B (Infinity War). 2020s: $2.33B (Avatar Way of Water) to $1.92B (Spider-Man NWH). 1989 Indiana Jones Last Crusade has range gross $474-494M in master; lower bound used consistently, placing LC below ROTJ as #4 of 1980s (out of scope) and keeping ROTJ as #3 of 1980s. Range-value handling documented in normalization_decisions and open_questions per cycle-2 lesson from antarctic-stations (normalization_decisions + open_questions seeded at cycle-0).
